newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Timorese killed under UN envoy's nose, says Horta.
newsitem.headline: Timorese killed under UN envoy's nose, says Horta.

text.p: East Timor independence leader Jose Ramos Horta said he had evidence Indonesian troops killed four students who brought a petition last month to the hotel of a U.N. special envoy.

The Nobel Peace laureate said among them were two of 33 East Timorese youths detained for several days for breaking into the Austrian embassy in Jakarta in a bid to see U.N. envoy Jamsheed Marker. They were murdered soon after their release a week ago, he said.

"I have with me photographic evidence of the Indonesian army's recent brutality," he said in a speech delivered on his behalf by the Pax Christi non-governmental organisation on Wednesday to the U.N. Human Rights Commission meeting in Geneva.
"This happened right under the nose of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General," said Horta, who left Geneva on Tuesday.

Horta, co-winner of the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize with Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo, said he was confident the 53-member forum would adopt a European Union resolution criticising abuses in the former Portuguese colony annexed by Indonesia in 1976.
In his speech, Horta also provided more details of an incident on March 23 in the East Timor capital Dili in which Indonesian authorities had denied there were deaths or serious injuries.
He showed reporters photographs he said were dated March 27, purportedly showing youths wounded in the clash and being cared for in Dili.
"We now have evidence that four students were killed and at least 20 were seriously injured," Horta said in his speech. He added he had received a list of 19 people still missing since the incident.
